checks: Substituting λ=σβ/(1−u) in the exact overlap gives Vg(u). Twice differentiating u^d/(β−1+u) gives the three displayed coefficients, with a strictly positive constant term since β>1 and d≥2. Thus g+(1−u)g′ increases strictly on (0,1) and has endpoints 0 and 1.

The positive-part integrand has bounded λ difference quotient by ℓ. The left and right derivatives of Φ are the strict and weak threshold masses, respectively, so the exact differentiable formula makes the equality-level mass zero and gives the displayed derivatives and dual value.

The intersection T∩F_λ(T) has positive volume and its compact convex projection selects precisely the whole positive-length columns with r_e≤λ. Intersecting T with the inverse image of that projection is compact convex with exactly mass Φ′=b. Its roof cost attains the dual lower bound.

At b=V, a proper compact convex subset has strictly smaller volume. The integral of min(λℓ,h+U) increases to the actual T roof. Expanding the exact overlap to first order in 1/λ gives V[dσβ−(σ−1)], which equals Vσβg′(1).

For σ=1, g(u)=u^d yields the universal value exactly. For σ>1 and b<V the λ=β/(1−η) comparison is strict. At b=V the explicit excess is V(σ−1)(dβ−1)>0. Source 5e5b642b770e6623 §§4–6 retains both the sharp universal bound and the fixed-direction convex optimizer.
